item.text: A local search index preprocesses documents into structures such as inverted indexes and embeddings, enabling fast query-time retrieval. Searching every document from scratch scans and analyzes all content for each query, which is simpler but grows slow and costly as the corpus expands. Indexes require storage, update pipelines, and occasional rebuilds, and may briefly lag behind source changes. Full scans are more immediately consistent but usually impractical for large or interactive collections.
